awards.award_amount_text: Last-dollar award that, combined with other aid, covers tuition, mandatory fees and average on-campus housing and food, for up to eight semesters; college-specific course fees for architecture, business, engineering and nursing are not covered.
awards.eligibility_summary: Tennessee high school graduates admitted as first-time freshmen (or transfers) with family AGI of $40,000 or less and total family assets of $40,000 or less; FAFSA by UT Priority Filing Date each year.
awards.renewal_requirements: Continuous full-time enrollment in CPOS-eligible courses, annual FAFSA by UT's priority date, family household income of $60,000 or less, and participation in the Rocky Top Scholars program.
awards.residency_requirement: Tennessee resident; U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

awards.award_amount_text: Last-dollar award covering tuition and mandatory fees when combined with other federal, state and institutional aid.
awards.eligibility_summary: Tennessee residents who receive HOPE, file the FAFSA by the UT Priority Filing Date and complete the UT Promise application by December 15; combined parent/student AGI under $75,000 and assets under $75,000.
awards.renewal_requirements: Continuous full-time enrollment in CPOS-eligible courses, annual FAFSA by UT's priority date, continued HOPE eligibility, participation in the Rocky Top Scholars program, and eight volunteer service hours plus mentoring each semester.
awards.residency_requirement: Tennessee resident; U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

awards.eligibility_summary: Chancellor's Scholarship based on academic merit and leadership; four new recipients selected each spring. Minimum 31 ACT (1390 SAT) and 4.0 UT Core GPA.
awards.renewal_requirements: Cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher, reviewed each spring.

awards.test_requirement: ACT/SAT composite superscore tiers (writing not used); official scores received by May 15; only tests through December of the senior year count.
awards.award_amount_text: $3,000-$9,000 per year for four years by test tier.
awards.eligibility_summary: Admitted in-state first-year students with a minimum 3.8 UT Weighted Core GPA who apply for admission by January 5 of the senior year; must matriculate the fall immediately after graduating from a US high school; US citizen or permanent resident.
awards.renewal_requirements: Maintain a 3.0 cumulative GPA, federal Satisfactory Academic Progress and full-time enrollment each semester.

awards.award_amount_text: $1,500 per year, up to $6,000 over four years.
awards.eligibility_summary: In-state students who complete the five-year Next Chapter program, apply by January 5 of the senior year and enroll the following fall. Must enroll the fall immediately after graduating from a US high school; U.S. citizen, permanent resident or domestic international student.
awards.renewal_requirements: Maintain a 3.0 cumulative GPA, full-time enrollment throughout each semester, and Satisfactory Academic Progress.

awards.eligibility_summary: Chancellor's Scholarship based on academic merit and leadership; six new recipients each year selected by the UT General Scholarship Committee. Minimum 31 ACT (1390 SAT) and 4.0 UT Core GPA.
awards.renewal_requirements: Cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher, reviewed each spring.

awards.award_amount_text: $5,000 per year for four years, or five years in standard five-year degree programs.
awards.eligibility_summary: Twenty-five entering students, including first-year and transfer students, are chosen annually based on academic merit, extracurricular/community activity, and creativity. Chancellor's Scholarships require a minimum 31 ACT (1390 SAT) and 4.0 UT Core GPA.
awards.renewal_requirements: Cumulative GPA of 3.25 or higher, reviewed at the end of each spring; a written appeal for extenuating circumstances may grant probationary eligibility for the next semester.

awards.award_name: Next Chapter Scholar of the Year Award
awards.award_amount_text: Tuition and mandatory fees for up to four years.
awards.eligibility_summary: One Tennessee senior selected annually by holistic review of the admission application and supplemental materials. Must enroll the fall immediately after graduating from a US high school; U.S. citizen, permanent resident or domestic international student.
awards.renewal_requirements: Maintain a 3.0 cumulative GPA, full-time enrollment throughout each semester, and Satisfactory Academic Progress.

awards.award_amount_text: Four-year awards of $5,000 annually to six new students; separate law-school and one-year variable awards exist.

awards.award_amount_text: Tuition and mandatory fees, renewable for four years.
awards.eligibility_summary: One top scholar from each of Tennessee's 95 counties; admitted in-state first-year students who apply by January 5 (November 1 priority) are automatically considered; minimum 3.2 UT core weighted GPA; holistic review.
awards.renewal_requirements: Maintain a 3.0 cumulative GPA, federal Satisfactory Academic Progress and full-time enrollment each semester.

appeals.deadline_text: Fall 2026: November 24, 2026; Spring 2027: March 5, 2027; Summer 2027: June 17, 2027.
appeals.contact_method: Vol Connect case, then MyUTK / CampusLogic forms.
appeals.process_summary: UT Knoxville publishes a central Financial Aid Appeals hub whose appeal types are Budget Increase, Dependency, HOPE & Institutional Scholarship, SAP, Special Circumstances and Teacher Licensure/Preparatory Course Certification. All documentation must be received at least 14 business days before the last day of classes for the appealed term; appeals not completed within 30 days of a documentation request are canceled.
The official Scholarship FAQ answers "Will UT match scholarship and financial aid offers from other institutions?" with "UT cannot match scholarship or aid offers from other institutions."

Budget Increase Appeals for additional education-related expenses (childcare, one-time computer purchase, internship/student teaching, one medical expense per year, extra books/supplies, study abroad). Excludes reimbursed expenses, amounts within the standard allowance, vehicle costs and expenses while not enrolled. Approval does not guarantee additional aid; decisions are final absent new documentation.

The HOPE & Institutional Scholarship Appeals route addresses loss of existing scholarship eligibility due to extenuating circumstances (enrollment drop, withdrawal, non-continuous enrollment, less than full-time, cumulative GPA). No official page reviewed documents a process for reconsidering or increasing an incoming merit award.

Dependency Appeals for a breakdown of the family support unit (e.g., abuse, severe estrangement, abandonment, parental incapacity or incarceration). Self-sufficiency, parental unwillingness to pay and non-claimed tax dependency do not qualify. Reviewed by the Appeal Committee after counselor screening.

appeals.contact_method: Vol Connect case, then MyUTK appeal form.
appeals.process_summary: Special Circumstances Appeals for documented financial changes since the FAFSA, such as loss/reduction of employment or income, loss of child support or benefits, divorce/separation, death of a parent or wage earner, unreimbursed medical expenses over 11% of AGI, one-time income events and retirement. One appeal per academic year (August-July); involuntary job-loss appeals wait at least 8 weeks after the event. Listed exclusions include standard living expenses, debts, multiple students in college, and fluctuating commission/self-employment income.
appeals.required_documents: Tax return transcript and all W-2s/1099s for student and parent (or spouse) plus assigned documentation.

appeals.process_summary: Satisfactory Academic Progress appeals to restore federal aid eligibility: personal statement (what happened, what changed, academic plan), third-party documentation and an advisor-signed academic plan; due at least 14 days before the last day of classes for the term.

HOPE & Institutional Scholarship Appeals: students may appeal loss of HOPE or institutional scholarship eligibility caused by extenuating circumstances (health emergency, death of immediate family member, mental health crisis). Dropping courses to protect GPA does not qualify. HOPE GPA review after a later benchmark and the one-time HOPE grade-replacement option are also handled here. Complete appeals (statement plus documentation) go to the Institutional Review Panel. Chancellor's Scholarship GPA-loss appeals can grant probationary eligibility for one semester.

rule_details.utrack: Full-time degree-seeking students must meet uTrack milestones in terms 1-5 (e.g., term 1: MATH 130/131 or higher; terms 3-4: engineering physics sequence; term 5: one listed intro course).
rule_details.progression: Progression to upper-division departmental programs is competitive and space-limited; factors include overall GPA, grades in required lower-division courses, and orderly progress without abuse of withdrawal/repeat privileges.
rule_details.five_year_bs_ms: Up to 9 graduate hours count toward both degrees; 3.4 GPA; conditional admission after 64 hours, full admission after 96 hours.
rule_details.grade_requirements: At least a C in every computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering and mathematics course used for the degree.
rule_details.prior_credit_notes: AP Computer Science A score of 3+ earns COSC 101; a departmental proficiency exam for COSC 101 is available on request.
rule_details.honors_concentration: Overall 3.4 GPA, four 100/200-level honors courses (14+ hours), two upper-division COSC/ECE honors courses and Cook Grand Challenge breadth requirements.
rule_details.engaged_inquiries_rule: Minimum of 9 credit hours in at least two subject areas.
rule_details.upper_division_electives_rule: Any 3XX/4XX COSC or ECE course not otherwise used, MATH 231, 241, 371, 471, 472; up to three COSC/ECE 5XX courses; COSC 322 does not count.
